title: Stuck or stranded in snow: stay safe
metaDesc: Stuck or stranded in snow? Stay with the car, clear the tailpipe before running the engine, run it only now and then, and watch for carbon monoxide.
first: Stay with your car. Don't try to walk for help in a storm.
Before you run the engine, clear snow away from the tailpipe. A blocked tailpipe can fill the car with carbon monoxide.
Run the engine only now and then, just long enough to stay warm. Crack a window while it runs.
Make the car easy to see: tie something bright to the antenna or window and keep the dome light on.
Call 911 if you're stranded, or anyone gets a headache, feels dizzy or sick, or is very sleepy.
dont: Don't run the engine for long with the windows up, or in a closed space like a garage.
Don't wear yourself out digging or pushing.

steps.t: If it's safe to get out, clear snow from around the tires and put sand or kitty litter in front of the wheels for grip. Go slowly.
A headache, dizziness, upset stomach, confusion or feeling very sleepy can mean carbon monoxide. Turn the engine off, get fresh air and call 911.
Use blankets and extra clothes, and drink water. Keep a winter kit in the car before you need it.

call: Call 911 if you're stranded, stuck in a traffic lane, or anyone shows signs of carbon monoxide.
If you're safely parked and just stuck, call roadside help for a tow out.

sources.t: North Dakota Highway Patrol: Frequently asked questions
